title.zh: 卷十六 志第八 百官
title.raw: 卷十六 志第八 百官 Volume 16 Treatises 8: Official Posts

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷十六‧志第八百官

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 16 — Treatise 8: Hundred Officials
translations.idiomatic: Volume 16 Treatises 8: Official Posts

sentences.zh: 建官設職，興自炎昊，方乎隆周之冊，表乎盛漢之書。

translations.literal: Establishing offices and setting posts arose from Yanhao; it appears in the registries of flourishing Zhou and is set forth in the books of Han at its height.
translations.idiomatic: The founding of offices began with the sage-kings of antiquity; it shows in the Zhou archives at their zenith and stands written in the Han histories at their flood.

sentences.zh: 存改回沿，備於歷代，先賢往學，以之雕篆者衆矣。

translations.literal: Preserved, altered, and carried forward, complete in successive ages; sages of old studied it, and many have carved it into writing.
translations.idiomatic: Kept, revised, and handed down through every dynasty, it drew generations of scholars—countless hands have cut it into stone and brush.

sentences.zh: 若夫胡廣舊儀，事惟簡撮，應劭官典，殆無遺恨。

translations.literal: As for Hu Guang's Old Protocols, the matters are only briefly excerpted; Ying Shao's Official Canon leaves scarcely any regret.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang's Old Protocols compress the record to essentials; Ying Shao's Official Canon leaves little wanting.

sentences.zh: 王朗奏議，屬霸國之初基；

translations.literal: Wang Lang's memorials and proposals belong to the founding of a hegemonic state;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang's memorials date to the first laying of a hegemon's foundations;

sentences.zh: 陳矯增曹，由軍事而補闕。

translations.literal: Chen Qiao's additions to the Cao offices came from military affairs to fill gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qiao's supplements to the Cao Wei roster grew out of war and patched what was missing.

sentences.zh: 今則有《魏氏官儀》、《魚豢中外官》也。

translations.literal: Now there are the "Official Protocols of the Wei House" and Yu Huan's "Central and Outer Officials."
translations.idiomatic: Today we have the Wei House's Official Protocols and Yu Huan's Central and Outer Officials.

sentences.zh: 山濤以意辯人，不囗囗囗。

translations.literal: Shan Tao judged men by his own sense, not [lacuna] [lacuna] [lacuna].
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao read men by intuition; the text is lost.

sentences.zh: 荀勗欲去事煩，唯論并省。

translations.literal: Xun Xu wished to strip away transactional tedium and discuss only merger and reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu wanted to cut the clutter of detail and speak only of consolidation.

sentences.zh: 定制成文，本之晉令，後代承業，案爲前准。

translations.literal: Fixed regulations made into written law take the Jin statutes as foundation; later generations inherit the enterprise and treat them as prior standards.
translations.idiomatic: Once rules were cast as written law they rested on the Jin code; later courts took up that work and made it their precedent.

sentences.zh: 肇域官品，區別階資，蔚宗選簿梗概，欽明階次詳悉，虞通、劉寅因荀氏之作，矯舊增新，今古相校。

translations.literal: At the inception official grades were delimited and ranks distinguished; Fan Ye's Selection Register gives the outline, the Qinming ranks in full detail; Yu Tong and Liu Yin, building on the Xun clan's work, rectified the old and added the new—past and present compared.
translations.idiomatic: When the hierarchy was first drawn, grades and ranks were sorted apart: Fan Ye's register sketches the frame, the Qinming text fills the ladder; Yu Tong and Liu Yin, following the Xun family's books, bent the old into the new—ancient and present set side by side.

sentences.zh: 齊受宋禪，事遵常典，旣有司存，無所偏廢。

translations.literal: Qi received Song's abdication; affairs follow the regular code; since the relevant offices exist, nothing was especially abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Qi took the throne from Song by abdication and kept the usual forms; where an office already stood, none was singled out for abolition.

sentences.zh: 其餘散在史注，多已筌拾，覽者易知，不重述也。

translations.literal: The rest scattered in historical notes has largely been gathered; readers may easily know them—not recounted again.
translations.idiomatic: What remains scattered through commentaries has mostly been gathered already; the reader can learn it elsewhere, so it is not told again here.

sentences.zh: 〈諸臺府郎令史職吏以下，具見長水校尉王珪之《職儀》。〉

translations.literal: 〈Clerks, recorders, and functionaries of the various bureaus and offices are fully set out in Colonel of the Long River Wang Guizhi's "Protocols of Office."〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈For clerks, recorders, and functionaries of the various bureaus and offices, see Colonel of the Long River Wang Guizhi's Protocols of Office.〉

translations.literal: Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor of State.

translations.literal: Since Xiao He and Cao Can, it has been the supreme rank for a minister.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiao He and Cao Can onward, it was the highest station a subject could hold.

translations.literal: In Song's Xiaojian era Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao held it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song, Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao held it in the Xiaojian era.

sentences.zh: 至齊不用人，以爲贈，不列官。

translations.literal: By Qi no one was appointed; it served as posthumous grant only and was not listed among active offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi no living man held it; it was given only as a posthumous honor and dropped from the active roster.

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 宋大明用江夏王義恭，以後無人。

translations.literal: In Song's Daming era Prince Yigong of Jiangxia held it; afterward no one.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Prince Yigong of Jiangxia held it in the Daming era; after that, no one.

translations.literal: Qi used it as posthumous grant.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi it was a posthumous title only.

translations.literal: Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor.

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, Grand Guardian, and Grand Tutor were Zhou old offices.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor, Grand Guardian, and Grand Tutor were offices of the Zhou.

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Dong Zhuo was Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Han, Dong Zhuo held the Grand Preceptorship.

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin Emperor Hui's reign, Wei Guan was Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jin Huidi's reign, Wei Guan was made Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 自後無太師，而太保爲贈。

translations.literal: Afterward there was no Grand Preceptor, and Grand Guardian became posthumous.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter no one held Grand Preceptor; Grand Guardian survived only as a posthumous grant.

translations.literal: Qi established only the Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Qi kept only the Grand Tutor among them.

translations.literal: Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal.

translations.literal: Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉用彭城王義康，後無人。

translations.literal: In Song's Yuanjia era Prince Yikang of Pengcheng held it; afterward no one.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's Yuanjia era Prince Yikang of Pengcheng held it; after that, no one.

translations.literal: Qi used it as posthumous grant.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi it was a posthumous title only.

translations.literal: Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant.

translations.literal: Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education.

translations.literal: Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works.

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies were formerly general offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies were once standing posts open to appointment.

sentences.zh: 司徒府領天下州郡名數戶口簿籍。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education's office oversaw registers of household names and population ledgers for all provinces and commanderies under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education's bureau kept the empire's registers of place-names, household counts, and population rolls.

sentences.zh: 雖無，常置左右長史、左西曹掾屬、主簿、祭酒、令史以下。

translations.literal: Though vacant, the left and right senior recorders, western-bureau aides-attendant, chief clerk, libationer, and recorders were always installed.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the seat was empty, left and right senior recorders, western-bureau aides, chief clerk, libationer, and recorders below them were always in place.

sentences.zh: 晉世王導爲司徒，右長史干寶撰立官府，《職儀》已具。

translations.literal: In Jin times Wang Dao served as Minister of Education; right senior recorder Gan Bao compiled the establishment of the government office—the "Protocols of Office" are complete.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin, Wang Dao was Minister of Education; his right senior recorder Gan Bao drew up the office establishment—the Protocols of Office already cover it.

translations.literal: Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: Special Advance.

translations.literal: Rank secondary to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Rank equal to a duke.

translations.literal: All Acting Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: All holders of Acting Three Excellencies.

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: General of Agile Cavalry.

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: General of Chariots and Cavalry.

translations.literal: General of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guard.

translations.literal: General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the Army.

translations.literal: General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Central Army.

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the Army.

translations.literal: Four Campaign Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Four Campaign Generals.

translations.literal: 〈East, West, South, North.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈East, West, South, North.〉

translations.literal: Four Garrison Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Four Garrison Generals.

sentences.zh: 凡諸將軍加「大」字，位從公。

translations.literal: Whenever generals had the character "Great" added, rank equaled a duke.
translations.idiomatic: Any general whose title took the prefix "Grand" ranked equal to a duke.

translations.literal: Opened-office honors ranked like a duke.
translations.idiomatic: An open office with honors equal to the three dukes ranked like a duke.

sentences.zh: 凡公督府置佐：長史、司馬各一人，諮議參軍二人。

translations.literal: Every duke's supervisory office set aides: one senior recorder and one marshal each, and two advising staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: Every duke-level commandery office appointed aides—one senior recorder and one marshal each, plus two advising staff officers.

sentences.zh: 諸曹有錄事，功曹，記室，戶曹，倉曹，中、直兵，外兵，騎兵，長流，賊曹，城局，法曹，田曹，水曹，鎧曹，集曹，右戶，十八曹。

translations.literal: The bureaus had recorders, merit clerks, secretaries, household clerks, granary clerks, central and direct military clerks, outer military clerks, cavalry clerks, long-service clerks, bandit-suppression clerks, city-office clerks, law clerks, field clerks, water clerks, armor clerks, assembly clerks, and right-household clerks—eighteen bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Its bureaus comprised recorders, merit clerks, secretaries, household and granary clerks, central and direct military sections, outer military and cavalry sections, long-service and bandit-suppression sections, city office, law, field, water, armor, assembly, and right-household sections—eighteen bureaus in all.

sentences.zh: 城局曹以上署正參軍，法曹以下署行參軍，各一人。

translations.literal: From the city-office bureau upward one regular staff officer was posted; from the law bureau downward one acting staff officer each.
translations.idiomatic: From the city-office bureau up, each post had a regular staff officer; from the law bureau down, an acting staff officer.

sentences.zh: 其行參軍無署者，爲長兼員。

translations.literal: Where an acting staff officer had no post, he served as long-term concurrent member.
translations.idiomatic: An acting staff officer without a dedicated post served as a standing concurrent appointee.

sentences.zh: 其府佐史則從事中郎二人，倉曹掾、戶曹屬、東西閤祭酒各一人，主簿舍人御屬二人。

translations.literal: The office aides and clerks were two attendant gentlemen, one granary bureau aide, one household bureau subordinate, one libationer each for the eastern and western pavilions, and two chief-clerk secretaries and imperial attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Office aides and clerks comprised two attendant gentlemen, a granary aide, a household subordinate, eastern and western pavilion libationers, and two chief-clerk secretaries with imperial attendants.

sentences.zh: 加崇者，則左右長史四人，中郎掾屬竝增數。

translations.literal: When honors were raised, there were four left and right senior recorders, and the attendant gentlemen and subordinates were increased in number.
translations.idiomatic: With added honors came four senior recorders, left and right, and more attendant gentlemen and subordinates.

sentences.zh: 其未及開府，則置府亦有佐史，其數有減。

translations.literal: Those not yet granted an open office still had office aides and clerks, but in reduced numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Even without an open office, a commandery staff kept aides and clerks—though fewer.

sentences.zh: 小府無長流，置禁防參軍。

translations.literal: Small offices had no long-service bureau; they posted a garrison-defense staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Small staffs omitted the long-service bureau and posted a garrison-defense staff officer instead.

translations.literal: Four Pacification Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Four Pacification Generals.

translations.literal: Four Tranquility Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Four Tranquility Generals.

translations.literal: Generals of the Left, Right, Front, and Rear.
translations.idiomatic: Generals of the Left, Right, Front, and Rear.

translations.literal: General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Subdues the Barbarians.

translations.literal: Four Central Guard Commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Four Central Guard Commandants.

sentences.zh: 晉世荀羨、王胡之竝居此官。

translations.literal: In Jin times Xun Xian and Wang Huzhi both held this office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin, Xun Xian and Wang Huzhi both held the post.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊以來，唯處諸王，素族無爲者。

translations.literal: Since Song and Qi, only imperial princes received it; no common clan ever did.
translations.idiomatic: From Song and Qi onward it went only to imperial princes; no commoner clan ever held it.

translations.literal: General Who Champions.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Champions.

translations.literal: General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Assists the State.

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the North.

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the Distance.

translations.literal: Dragon-Courser General.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-Courser General.

translations.literal: Among these lesser titles, some also had offices established.
translations.idiomatic: Even some of these lesser titles could open a full staff office.

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 府置丞一人，五官、功曹、主簿，九府九史皆然。

translations.literal: The office had one deputy, plus five officers, merit clerk, and chief clerk—the nine ministries and nine clerks were all alike.
translations.idiomatic: Its office had one deputy, five officers, a merit clerk, and a chief clerk—the same pattern as the other eight ministries and their clerks.

translations.literal: Subordinate offices are as follows:
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw the following posts:

translations.literal: Erudites—called erudites of the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites, styled erudites of the Grand Academy.

translations.literal: One director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: One director of the Imperial Academy.

translations.literal: Two erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Two erudites.

translations.literal: Ten teaching assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Ten teaching assistants.

sentences.zh: 建元四年，有司奏置國學，祭酒准諸曹尚書，博士准中書郎，助教准南臺御史。

translations.literal: In Jianyuan year 4 the relevant offices memorialized to establish the national academy: the director's rank equaled directors of the masters of writing in other bureaus, erudites equaled secretariat gentlemen, and assistants equaled censors of the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 4 the ministries proposed a national academy: its director ranked with a bureau director of the masters of writing, its erudites with a secretariat gentleman, its assistants with a Southern Bureau censor.

translations.literal: Classical learning came first in selection.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates were chosen first for mastery of the classics.

sentences.zh: 若其人難備，給事中以還明經者，以本位領。

translations.literal: If suitable men were hard to find, a palace attendant who had passed the classics examination might lead in his existing post.
translations.idiomatic: When no one qualified could be found, a palace attendant who had passed the classics examination might serve concurrently in his present rank.

sentences.zh: 其下典學二人，三品，准太常主簿；

translations.literal: Below them were two academy directors, third rank, equivalent to the Minister of Ceremonies' chief clerk;
translations.idiomatic: Below them stood two academy directors of third rank, equal to the Minister of Ceremonies' chief clerk;

translations.literal: two household clerks and two ritual clerks each, fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: two household clerks and two ritual clerks each, fifth rank;

translations.literal: eight white-register clerks for ritual administration, sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: eight white-register clerks for ritual paperwork, sixth rank;

translations.literal: two academy physicians;
translations.idiomatic: two academy physicians;

translations.literal: two masters of ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: two masters of ceremony.

sentences.zh: 其夏，國諱廢學，有司奏省助教以下。

translations.literal: That summer, because of the imperial mourning taboo the schools were suspended; the ministries memorialized to abolish posts below teaching assistant.
translations.idiomatic: That summer mourning for the late emperor closed the schools; the ministries proposed cutting every post below teaching assistant.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，立學，尚書令王儉領祭酒。

translations.literal: In Yongming year 3 the academy was re-established; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian headed it as director.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 3 the academy was restored; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian served as its director.

sentences.zh: 八年，國子博士何胤單爲祭酒，疑所服，陸澄等皆不能據，遂以玄服臨試。

translations.literal: In year 8 the academy erudite He Yin alone became director; uncertain what robes to wear, Lu Cheng and others could cite no precedent, so he presided over examinations in black garb.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the academy erudite He Yin became sole director; with no precedent for his robes, Lu Cheng and the rest could not decide, and he examined candidates in black dress.

sentences.zh: 月餘日，博議定，乃服朱衣。

translations.literal: After a month and more of broad deliberation, he donned vermilion robes.
translations.idiomatic: After a month of debate among scholars, he took vermilion robes.

translations.literal: One director of the Zongming Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: One director of the Zongming Observatory.

sentences.zh: 右太始六年，以國學廢，初置總明觀，玄、儒、文、史四科，科置學士各十人，正令史一人，書令史二人，幹一人，門吏一人，典觀吏二人。

translations.literal: Note: In Taishi year 6, when the national academy was abolished, the Zongming Observatory was first established—four disciplines, Daoist, Confucian, literary, and historical, each with ten scholars; one chief recorder, two document recorders, one steward, one gate officer, and two observatory clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Note: In Taishi 6, with the national academy shut, the Zongming Observatory was founded—Daoist, Confucian, literary, and historical sections, ten scholars each; plus one chief recorder, two document recorders, a steward, a gate officer, and two observatory clerks.

translations.literal: During Jianyuan it oversaw the five rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianyuan era it managed the five rites.

translations.literal: In Yongming year 3 the national academy was built, and it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the national academy reopened in Yongming 3, the observatory was abolished.

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, one; deputy, one.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, one; deputy, one.

translations.literal: Director of the Bright Hall, one; deputy, one.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Bright Hall, one; deputy, one.

translations.literal: Director of Imperial Sacrifices, one; deputy, one.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Imperial Sacrifices, one; deputy, one.

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Astronomer, one; deputy, one.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Astronomer, one; deputy, one.

translations.literal: Director of Sacrificial Victims: one; aide: one.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Sacrificial Victims: one; aide: one.

translations.literal: Below the director and aide, all had functional clerks appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Below the director and aide, functional clerks were all appointed.

translations.literal: Grand Musician: one; aide: one.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Musician: one; aide: one.

translations.literal: Directors of the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Directors of the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 永明末置，用二品三品勳。

translations.literal: Established at the end of Yongming; men of second- and third-rank merit were used.
translations.idiomatic: Established at the end of Yongming; appointees were drawn from holders of second- and third-rank merit.

sentences.zh: 置主簿、戶曹各一人，六品保舉。

translations.literal: One registrar and one household-section chief were appointed; selections were nominated at rank six.
translations.idiomatic: One registrar and one household-section chief were appointed; candidates were nominated at rank six.

translations.literal: Supervisor of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of Attendants.

translations.literal: The bureau had one aide.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau had one aide.

translations.literal: Offices under charge are as follows:
translations.idiomatic: Offices under its charge are as follows:

translations.literal: Left and Right Grand Masters of Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Grand Masters of Splendor.

sentences.zh: 位從公，開府置佐史如公。

translations.literal: Rank equivalent to a duke; they opened a bureau and appointed aides and clerks as for a duke.
translations.idiomatic: Rank equivalent to a duke; they opened a bureau and appointed aides and clerks like a duke.

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Splendor.

sentences.zh: 皆銀章青綬，詔加金章紫綬者，爲金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: All had silver seals and green ribbons; those whom an edict added a golden seal and purple ribbon became Grand Masters of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: All bore silver seals and green ribbons; when an edict added a golden seal and purple ribbon, the holder became a Grand Master of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 樂安任遐爲光祿，就王晏乞一片金，晏乃啓轉爲金紫，不行。

translations.literal: Ren Xia of Le'an was grand master of splendor; he asked Wang Yan for a piece of gold, and Yan memorialized to transfer him to golden seal and purple ribbon, but it did not go through.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xia of Le'an held the grand mastership of splendor; he asked Wang Yan for a piece of gold, and Yan memorialized to promote him to golden seal and purple ribbon, but the request failed.

translations.literal: Superior Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Superior Grand Master of the Palace.

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 諸大夫官，皆處舊齒老年，重者加親信二十人。

translations.literal: For all these grand-master posts, men of old standing and advanced years were placed; for the weightier posts, twenty personal attendants were added.
translations.idiomatic: These grand-master posts went to men of long service and advanced years; for the more honored posts, twenty personal attendants were added.

translations.literal: Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the Guards.

translations.literal: The bureau had one aide.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau had one aide.

translations.literal: He oversaw the palace city's gates and keys.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the palace city's gates and keys.

sentences.zh: 張衡西京賦曰「衞尉八屯，警夜巡晝」。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng's Western Capital Rhapsody says, 「The Commandant of the Guards' eight garrisons—alert at night, patrol by day.」
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's Western Capital Rhapsody says, 「The commandant of the guards' eight garrisons—alert at night, patrol by day.」

sentences.zh: 宮城諸却敵樓上本施鼓，持夜者以應更唱，太祖以鼓多驚眠，改以鐵磬云。

translations.literal: On all the parapet towers of the palace city drums had originally been installed; night watchmen answered the change of watch by drumming. The Founder, finding the drums often startled sleep, changed them to iron chimes, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: On every parapet tower of the palace city drums had once been set up, and night watchmen answered the watch-change call with them. The Founder, saying the drums too often broke sleep, is said to have replaced them with iron chimes.

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 府置丞一人，正一人，監一人，評一人，律博士一人。

translations.literal: The bureau had one aide, one chief judge, one inspector, one reviewer, and one doctor of law.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau had one aide, one chief judge, one inspector, one reviewer, and one doctor of law.

translations.literal: Grand Minister of Agriculture.

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yulin was made heir, Empress Dowager Wen'an assumed her honorific title, and these posts were established bearing palace names.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin was made heir and Empress Dowager Wen'an took her honorific title, these offices were created and named after palace quarters.

translations.idiomatic: Grand Chamberlain for the Palace Environs.

translations.idiomatic: Recorder of the masters of writing.

translations.idiomatic: Director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 總領尚書臺二十曹，爲內臺主。

translations.literal: He oversaw all twenty departments of the Masters-of-Writing Secretariat and was chief of the inner office.
translations.idiomatic: He headed all twenty departments of the secretariat and served as chief of the inner office.

translations.literal: When he traveled on the road, everyone from princes downward had to halt.
translations.idiomatic: On the road, everyone from princes down had to stop and make way.

translations.literal: The left and right vice directors traveled by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right vice directors used separate routes.

sentences.zh: 無令，左僕射爲臺主，與令同。

translations.literal: When there was no director, the left vice director was head of the secretariat, with the same authority as the director.
translations.idiomatic: If the directorate was vacant, the left vice director headed the secretariat with the director's authority.

translations.literal: Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice director.

sentences.zh: 領殿中主客二曹事，諸曹郊廟、園陵、車駕行幸、朝儀、臺內非違、文官舉補滿敘疾假事，其諸吉慶瑞應衆賀、災異賊發衆變、臨軒崇拜、改號格制、莅官銓選，凡諸除署、功論、封爵、貶黜、八議、疑讞、通關案，則左僕射主，右僕射次經，維是黃案，左僕射右僕射署朱符見字，經都丞竟，右僕射橫畫成目，左僕射畫，令畫。

translations.literal: He oversaw the Palace and Guest-Relations departments. For all departments—suburban and temple sacrifices, imperial tombs, imperial progresses, court ritual, internal secretariat violations, civil appointments, promotions, completed tenure, and sick leave; and for all congratulatory rites for auspicious omens, mass felicitations, disasters, bandit outbreaks, and collective emergencies, imperial-audience worship, changes of era titles and regulations, arrival at post and selection of officers, and every appointment, merit evaluation, enfeoffment, demotion, eight deliberations, doubtful cases, and transit permits—the left vice director took primary responsibility and the right vice director handled secondary routing. For yellow documents, the left and right vice directors affixed red seals and visible endorsements; after the secretariat aide completed review, the right vice director drew a horizontal stroke to close the entry, the left vice director signed, and the director signed.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Palace and Guest-Relations bureaus. Across the departments he took the lead on suburban and temple rites, imperial tombs, progresses, court ceremony, internal discipline, civil appointments and promotions, completed terms, and sick leave; on congratulatory rites for good omens, mass celebrations, disasters, rebellions, and other emergencies; on imperial-audience worship, era-title and regulatory changes, and arrival and selection of officials; and on every appointment, merit review, enfeoffment, demotion, eight deliberations, doubtful case, and transit permit—the left vice director led and the right vice director followed. On yellow documents both vice directors applied red seals and visible endorsements; after the secretariat aide finished review, the right vice director drew a horizontal closing stroke, then the left vice director and the director signed.

translations.literal: If the right-hand official was absent, the next in order signed jointly.
translations.idiomatic: If the official on the right was absent, the next in line signed together.

sentences.zh: 若無左右，則直置僕射在其中閒，總左右事。

translations.literal: If there were neither left nor right, a single vice director was placed between them to oversee both sides' duties.
translations.idiomatic: If neither left nor right vice director was in place, one vice director was appointed between them to handle both sides.

translations.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 領吏部、刪定、三公、比部四曹。

translations.literal: He oversaw the Personnel, Revision, Three Excellencies, and Comparison departments.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Personnel, Revision, Three Excellencies, and Comparison bureaus.

translations.idiomatic: Minister of revenue.

translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Justice, Water, Stores, and Merit-Evaluation bureaus.

translations.idiomatic: Minister of the five armies.

translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the Inner and Outer Military bureaus.

translations.idiomatic: Minister of the sacrificial department.

translations.idiomatic: Minister of construction.

translations.idiomatic: Created temporarily to erect palaces and temples, then abolished when the work ended.

translations.literal: Left aide, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Left aide, one person.

sentences.zh: 掌宗廟郊祠、吉慶瑞應、災異、立作格制、諸案彈、選用除置、吏補滿除遣注職。

translations.literal: He handled suburban and temple sacrifices, auspicious omens and congratulatory rites, disasters and anomalies, new regulations, case reviews and impeachments, appointments and dismissals, filling vacancies, and assigning posts.
translations.idiomatic: He handled suburban and temple sacrifices, auspicious omens and congratulatory rites, disasters and anomalies, new regulations, case reviews and impeachments, appointments and dismissals, filling vacancies, and posting officials to duty.

translations.literal: Right aide, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Right aide, one person.

sentences.zh: 掌兵士百工補役死叛考代年老疾病解遣、其內外諸庫藏穀帛、刑辠創業諍訟、田地船乘、稟拘兵工死叛、考剔討補、差分百役、兵器諸營署人領、州郡租布、民戶移徙、州郡縣併帖、城邑民戶割屬、刺史二千石令長丞尉被收及免贈、文武諸犯削官事。

translations.literal: He handled soldiers and artisans—recruitment, replacements for death and desertion, evaluations, release for age, illness, or disability; all internal and external granaries and treasuries of grain and silk; criminal cases, land disputes, and lawsuits; fields, boats, and transport; conscription of laborers who died or deserted, assessments, replacements, and allocation of corvée; arms, garrison personnel, and workshop staffing; provincial and commandery tax deliveries in cloth; household migration; mergers of provinces, commanderies, and counties; reassignment of urban households; arrest, dismissal, reward, or posthumous honors for inspectors, two-thousand-shi officials, magistrates, aides, and commandants; and all civil and military cases involving stripping of office.
translations.idiomatic: He handled soldiers and artisans—recruitment, replacements for the dead and deserters, evaluations, and release for age, sickness, or disability; grain and silk in state storehouses inside and out; criminal, property, and litigation matters; land, boats, and transport; laborers who died or fled service, review, replacement, and corvée assignment; arms, camps, and workshop staffing; provincial and commandery cloth taxes; household moves; mergers of provinces, commanderies, and counties; reassignment of city populations; arrest, removal, reward, or posthumous honors for inspectors, two-thousand-shi officials, and county magistrates, aides, and commandants; and every civil or military case that stripped an office.

sentences.zh: 白案，右丞上署，左丞次署。

translations.literal: For white documents, the right aide signed first and the left aide second.
translations.idiomatic: On white documents the right aide signed first and the left aide second.

sentences.zh: 黃案，左丞上署，右丞次署。

translations.literal: For yellow documents, the left aide signed first and the right aide second.
translations.idiomatic: On yellow documents the left aide signed first and the right aide second.

sentences.zh: 諸立格制及詳讞大事宗廟朝廷儀體，左丞上署，右丞次署。

translations.literal: For all new regulations and major reviewed cases concerning ancestral temples and court ceremonial, the left aide signed first and the right aide second.
translations.idiomatic: For new regulations and major reviewed cases on ancestral temples and court ritual, the left aide signed first and the right aide second.

sentences.zh: 自令僕以下五尚書八座二十曹，各置郎中令史以下，又置都令史分領之。

translations.literal: From the director and vice directors down through the five ministers, eight seats, and twenty departments, each had gentleman-attendants and clerks; chief clerks were also appointed to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: From the director and vice directors through the five ministers, eight seats, and twenty bureaus, each office had gentlemen-attendants and clerks below them, with chief clerks assigned to supervise.

sentences.zh: 僕射掌朝軌，尚書掌讞奏，都丞任碎，在彈違諸曹緣常及外詳讞事。

translations.literal: The vice directors managed court protocol; the directors handled memorials; the secretariat aides handled detail, rebuking violations in routine department matters and external case review.
translations.idiomatic: Vice directors managed court protocol, directors handled memorials, and secretariat aides handled detail—checking routine violations in the bureaus and reviewing outside cases.

sentences.zh: 應須命議相值者，皆郎先立意，應奏黃案及關事，以立意官爲議主。

translations.literal: When deliberation was required, gentlemen-attendants first drafted the position; for yellow-document memorials and related matters, the drafting officer chaired discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When consultation was needed, gentlemen-attendants drafted the proposal first; for yellow-document memorials and related business, the drafter chaired the discussion.

sentences.zh: 凡辭訴有漫命者，曹緣諮如舊。

translations.literal: For all petitions lacking clear orders, departments consulted as before.
translations.idiomatic: Petitions with vague instructions were routed through the bureaus as before.

sentences.zh: 若命有諮，則以立意者爲議主。

translations.literal: If the order required consultation, the drafting officer chaired discussion.
translations.idiomatic: If the order called for consultation, the drafter chaired the discussion.

translations.idiomatic: He answered to the Department of Mobilization and also to the Office of the Army.

translations.literal: Chief of the Gentlemen-in-Attendance of the Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Chief of the gentlemen-in-attendance of the palace gate.

translations.literal: 〈So titled for those of highest merit.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈So titled for those of highest merit.〉

translations.literal: Gentlemen-in-Attendance of the Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen-in-attendance of the palace gate.

translations.literal: In Han times it was an intimate post at court.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han it was a post kept close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉選用，稍增華重，而大意不異。

translations.literal: Under Wei and Jin selection it gained a little more splendor and weight, but the essential character did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin made the appointment somewhat grander, yet its heart stayed the same.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉中，王華、王曇首、殷景仁等，竝爲侍中，情在親密，與帝接膝共語，貂拂帝手，拔貂置案上，語畢復手插之。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen of Song, Wang Hua, Wang Tan-shou, Yin Jingren, and others all served as gentlemen-in-attendance; close in feeling, they spoke with the emperor knee to knee, brushed the imperial hand with their sable, drew the sable off and laid it on the table, and when speech was done slipped their hands back in.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wen of Song's Yuanjia years Wang Hua, Wang Tan-shou, Yin Jingren, and others served together as gentlemen-in-attendance, intimate enough to talk knee to knee with the emperor—brushing his hand with their sable, slipping it off to lay on the table, then, when words were spent, sliding their hands back in.

sentences.zh: 孝武時，侍中何偃南郊陪乘，鑾輅過白門閫，偃將匐，帝乃接之曰：「朕乃陪卿。

translations.literal: In the Xiaowu era the gentleman-in-attendance He Yan rode beside the emperor at the southern suburb; when the imperial carriage passed the White Gate barbican Yan was about to prostrate himself, and the emperor caught him up, saying, "I shall accompany you."
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu, He Yan, gentleman-in-attendance, rode beside the emperor at the southern suburb; as the train passed the White Gate barbican he was about to bow flat, and the emperor stayed him: "I shall keep you company."

sentences.zh: 」齊世朝會，多以美姿容者兼官。

translations.literal: In Qi, court assemblies often gave concurrent posts to men of handsome bearing.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi, court levees often doubled handsome men in other offices.

sentences.zh: 永元三年，東昏南郊，不欲親朝士，以主璽陪乘，前代未嘗有也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongyuan, when Emperor Donghun went to the southern suburb he would not face the court gentlemen and had the Keeper of the Imperial Seal ride beside him—something no earlier age had done.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan's third year Emperor Donghun, going to the southern suburb, refused to face the court gentlemen and set the keeper of the imperial seal beside him in the carriage—a thing no age before had seen.

translations.literal: The gentlemen-in-attendance were called "Gate Below."
translations.idiomatic: In court speech they were called "Gate Below."

translations.literal: Clerk-recorders were also appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk-recorders were appointed as well.

translations.literal: Offices under its charge were as follows:
translations.idiomatic: Offices under its charge:

translations.literal: Gentlemen Attendants of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen attendants of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 亦管知詔令，世呼爲小門下。

translations.literal: Also in charge of edicts and orders; in common speech, "Lesser Gate Below."
translations.idiomatic: They also handled edicts and orders; courtiers called them "Lesser Gate Below."

translations.literal: Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Regular attendant-in-ordinary.

translations.literal: Direct Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Direct regular attendant-in-ordinary.

translations.literal: Supernumerary Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary regular attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 舊與侍中通官，其通直員外，用衰老人士，故其官漸替。

translations.literal: Formerly they shared office with the gentlemen-in-attendance; the direct and supernumerary posts were given to elderly men of standing, so the rank gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had shared rank with the gentlemen-in-attendance; direct and supernumerary posts went to aged men of note, and the office slowly hollowed out.

sentences.zh: 宋大明雖華選比侍中，而人情久習，終不見重，尋復如初。

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Song the selection was as splendid as for gentlemen-in-attendance, but long habit kept it from winning regard, and before long it returned to what it had been.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's Daming years the post was chosen with as much show as the gentlemen-in-attendance, yet custom had taught men not to esteem it, and soon it sank back to the old level.

translations.literal: Gentleman Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

translations.literal: Direct Gentleman Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Direct gentleman cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

translations.literal: Supernumerary Gentleman Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary gentleman cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen for palace service.

translations.idiomatic: Court attendants at imperial audience.

translations.literal: Commandant of the Horse-Consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the horse-consorts.

translations.literal: Duties of the Secretariat for Imperial Writings; chief clerks for documents were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Duties of the Secretariat for Imperial Writings; chief clerks for documents were posted.

sentences.zh: 朝散用衣冠之餘，人數猥積。

translations.literal: Court attendants at audience were drawn from the leavings of formal office; their numbers piled up without measure.
translations.idiomatic: Court attendants at audience were filled from men who had left the cap and gown; the rolls swelled past counting.

sentences.zh: 永明中，奉朝請至六百餘人。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era there were more than six hundred court attendants at audience.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yongming years court attendants at audience numbered more than six hundred.

sentences.zh: 中書監一人，令一人，侍郎四人，通事舍人無員。

translations.literal: Superintendent of the Palace Secretariat, one person; director, one person; four gentlemen-attendants; palace messengers without fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Superintendent of the palace secretariat, one; director, one; four gentlemen-attendants; palace messengers without fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 中書省職，置主書、令史、正書以下。

translations.literal: Duties of the Palace Secretariat; chief document clerks, clerk-recorders, document officers, and below were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Duties of the palace secretariat; chief document clerks, recorder-clerks, document officers, and ranks below were posted.

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Library, one person; aide, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the imperial library, one person; aide, one person.

translations.literal: Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman.

translations.literal: Assistant Gentleman for Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant gentleman for compilation.

sentences.zh: 晉祕書閣有令史，掌衆書，見《晉令》，令亦置令史、正書及弟子，皆典教書畫。

translations.literal: Under Jin the library pavilion had clerk-recorders in charge of all books, as in the Jin statutes; the director also appointed clerk-recorders, document officers, and disciples, all charged with teaching writing and painting.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin the library pavilion kept clerk-recorders over all books, per the Jin statutes; the director likewise posted clerk-recorders, document officers, and disciples, all to teach writing and painting.

translations.literal: Inspector-in-Chief of the Censorate, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector-in-chief of the censorate, one person.

sentences.zh: 晉江左中丞司隷分督百僚，傅咸所云「行馬內外」是也。

translations.literal: Under Jin east of the Yangzi the inspector-in-chief and the director of the capital shared oversight of the hundred officials—what Fu Xian called "running horses inside and out."
translations.idiomatic: East of the Yangzi under Jin the inspector-in-chief and the capital director split supervision of the hundred officials—Fu Xian's "running horses inside and out."

sentences.zh: 今中丞則職無不察，專道而行，騶輻禁呵，加以聲色，武將相逢，輙致侵犯，若有鹵簿，至相敺擊。

translations.literal: Today the inspector-in-chief has no matter he does not examine; he travels in his own lane, with outriders and guards shouting him clear, voice and display together; when he meets military officers they often trespass, and if there is an imperial train they may come to blows.
translations.idiomatic: Now the inspector-in-chief looks into everything; he keeps his own road, outriders and guards shouting the way clear, pomp and voice together. Military men who meet him often clash; where an imperial train passes, blows may be exchanged.

sentences.zh: 宋孝建二年制，中丞與尚書令分道，雖丞郎下朝相值，亦得斷之，餘內外衆官，皆受停駐。

translations.literal: A regulation of the second year of Xiaojian in Song: the inspector-in-chief and the director of the masters of writing used separate routes; even when aides and gentlemen met him leaving court they might halt him, and all other officials inside and out had to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Xiaojian second year fixed that the inspector-in-chief and the director of the masters of writing took different roads; even aides and gentlemen meeting him after court could be stopped, and every other officer within or without had to pull aside.

translations.literal: Gentlemen for Legal Documents, two persons.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen for legal documents, two persons.

translations.literal: Gentlemen Attendants of the Censorate, ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen attendants of the censorate, ten persons.

sentences.zh: 蘭臺置諸曹內外督令以下。

translations.literal: The Orchid Terrace set up the various bureaus' internal and external overseers, commanders, and below.
translations.idiomatic: The Orchid Terrace posted internal and external overseers, commanders, and ranks below for the various bureaus.

translations.literal: Superintendent of the Receptionists, one person.
translations.idiomatic: Superintendent of the receptionists, one person.

translations.literal: Receptionists, ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: Receptionists, ten persons.

translations.literal: The Receptionists' Office managed court audiences and guest banquets.
translations.idiomatic: The Receptionists' Office handled court audiences and banquets for guests.

translations.literal: General Who Leads the Army; General of the Central Army Who Leads the Army.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Leads the Army; General of the Central Army Who Leads the Army.

translations.idiomatic: General Who Protects the Army; General of the Central Army Who Protects the Army.

translations.literal: Any post with zhong, xiao, or qing is the same office.
translations.idiomatic: Posts marked central, minor, or light were the same office.

translations.literal: All who held general posts showed respect to the Army Lead and Protect generals.
translations.idiomatic: Every general had to show deference to the Army Lead and Protect generals.

sentences.zh: 諸王爲將軍，道相逢，則領、護讓道。

translations.literal: When princes who were generals met on the road, the Army Lead and Protect generals yielded the road.
translations.idiomatic: If a prince holding a generalship met them on the road, the Army Lead and Protect generals gave way.

sentences.zh: 置長史、司馬、五官、功曹、主簿。

translations.literal: They appointed a senior recorder, marshal, five officers, merit clerk, and registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had a senior recorder, marshal, five officers, merit clerk, and registrar.

translations.idiomatic: Left and right guard generals.

translations.idiomatic: Valiant Cavalry General.

translations.idiomatic: Roving General.

sentences.zh: 晉世以來，謂領、護至驍、游爲六軍。

translations.literal: From Jin times onward, Army Lead and Protect through Valiant Cavalry and Roving were called the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin, the Army Lead and Protect posts through Valiant Cavalry and Roving were known as the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 二衞置司馬次官功曹主簿以下。

translations.literal: The two guards offices had marshals, deputy staff officers, merit clerks, and registrars and below.
translations.idiomatic: The two guard offices appointed marshals, deputy staff officers, merit clerks, and registrars and below.

translations.idiomatic: Left and right central gentlemen of the suite.

sentences.zh: 前軍將軍、後軍將軍、左軍將軍、右軍將軍，號四軍。

translations.literal: Front Army General, Rear Army General, Left Army General, and Right Army General—called the Four Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Front, rear, left, and right army generals—called the Four Armies.

sentences.zh: 屯騎、步兵、射聲、越騎、長水五校尉。

translations.idiomatic: Commandants of escort cavalry, footsoldiers, volley sound, crossbow cavalry, and long water—the five commandants.

sentences.zh: 自二衞、四軍、五校已下，謂之「西省」，而散騎爲「東省」。

translations.idiomatic: From the two guards, four armies, and five commandants down was the Western Bureau; attendant cavalier posts formed the Eastern Bureau.

translations.idiomatic: Intendant of Danyang.

translations.idiomatic: Junior tutor.

translations.idiomatic: Director of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 太子翊軍步兵屯騎三校尉。

translations.idiomatic: Crown prince's supporting army, footsoldiers, and escort cavalry commandants.

translations.idiomatic: On the right: Eastern Palace staff.

translations.literal: Provincial governors and inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors and inspectors.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉世州牧隆重，刺史任重者爲使持節都督，輕者爲持節督，起漢從帝時，御史中丞馮赦討九江賊，督揚、徐二州軍事，而何、徐《宋志》云起魏武遣諸州將督軍，王珪之《職儀》云起光武，竝非也。

translations.literal: In Wei and Jin times provincial governors were weighty; inspectors with heavy duty became commissioners bearing the staff of authority and overseers, lighter ones commissioners bearing the staff of authority and supervisors. It began in the time of the Following Han emperor, when Inspector-General Feng She suppressed bandits in Jiujiang and oversaw military affairs in Yang and Xu provinces; yet the He and Xu Song Gazetteer says it began when Cao Cao sent generals of the provinces to oversee armies, and Wang Guizhi's Protocol of Offices says it began with Guangwu—all are wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and Jin, provincial governors were honored posts; inspectors with heavy responsibility became commissioners bearing the staff of authority and military overseers, lighter ones commissioners bearing the staff and supervisors. The office began under the Following Han emperor, when Inspector-General Feng She campaigned against Jiujiang bandits and directed Yang and Xu military affairs; but the He and Xu Song Gazetteer dates it to Cao Cao's dispatch of provincial generals to oversee troops, and Wang Guizhi's Protocol of Offices to Emperor Guangwu—all are mistaken.

sentences.zh: 晉太康中，都督知軍事，刺史治民，各用人。

translations.literal: In Jin Taikang, the overseer handled military affairs and the inspector governed the people; each had his own appointees.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Taikang the military overseer commanded troops and the inspector governed the people, each with separate staffs.

sentences.zh: 惠帝末，乃幷任，非要州則單爲刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Hui's reign the two posts were merged; unless it was a key province, one person alone served as regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Emperor Hui the two offices were combined; save in a vital province, a man held the inspectorate alone.

sentences.zh: 州朝置別駕、治中、議曹、文學祭酒、諸曹部從事史。

translations.literal: Each province had a chief administrator, registrar, deliberation office, libationer of letters and literature, and section clerks for the various departments.
translations.idiomatic: At every provincial court stood a chief administrator, a registrar, a deliberation bureau, a libationer of letters and learning, and the section clerks of the various departments.

translations.idiomatic: Commandant Protecting the Southern Barbarians.

translations.idiomatic: Commandant Protecting the Three Ba.

translations.idiomatic: Established in Song.

translations.idiomatic: District magistrates and chancellors.

translations.idiomatic: Where a commandery or district was a princedom, the posts were interior minister and chancellor.

translations.idiomatic: Army Protector Garrisoning the Barbarians.

translations.idiomatic: Army Protector Pacifying the Distance.

translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous titles of Jin times; many were borne by men who headed their commanderies.

translations.literal: For each prince: one teacher, one friend, and one man of letters.
translations.idiomatic: Each prince had one teacher, one friend, and one literary adviser.

sentences.zh: 國官郎中令、中尉、大農爲三卿，左右常侍、侍郎，上軍、中軍、下軍三軍，典書、典祠、學官、典衞四令，食官、廄牧長、謁者以下。

translations.literal: Princedom offices: the Director of the Palace, the Commandant, and the Grand Agronomist as three ministers; left and right regular attendants and gentlemen-attendants; upper, middle, and lower armies as three armies; directors of documents, sacrifices, the academic office, and the guard as four directors; director of food, chief of stables and pastures, ushers, and below.
translations.idiomatic: A princedom kept a Director of the Palace, a Commandant, and a Grand Agronomist as its three ministers; left and right regular attendants and gentlemen-attendants; upper, middle, and lower armies; directors of documents, sacrifices, the academic office, and the guard; and below them the director of food, the chief of stables and pastures, ushers, and the rest.

translations.literal: For dukes and marquises, only the Director of the Palace as one minister.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and marquises kept only the Director of the Palace as their single minister.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：百司分置，惟皇命職。

translations.literal: In praise: the hundred offices are set apart in their posts; only the sovereign names their duties.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: the hundred bureaus stand divided in their stations; only the sovereign fixes their charge.

translations.literal: Cloud-master and bird-record—each has its proper pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Clouds, Recorder of Birds—each keeps its proper measure.

translations.idiomatic: [1] Endnote marker.
